informs: gloves and reusable bags/buckets
water / hydration for volunteers
first-aid kit recommendation

sources.title: Safety Guidelines for Beach / Shoreline Cleanup Activity
informs: closed-toe shoes; no bare hands
do not pick medical waste / syringes / needles
do not open bottles or unknown liquid containers
do not go into water; avoid culverts and drainage outlets
keep distance from oil drums; report to leader

sources.title: Community clean ups and litter picks
informs: gloves and bags as minimum kit
do not handle clinical waste / needles — note location and inform authority
avoid deep or fast-flowing water, steep banks, busy roads
avoid working alone when possible; tell someone your plan

sources.title: Community sharps management — found a sharp in public
informs: if you find a discarded sharp that is not yours, do not touch it
arrange safe removal via local authority / cleanup service

sources.title: DOs and DON'Ts of Proper Sharps Disposal
informs: do not throw loose sharps in trash or recycling
do not bend, break, or recap needles used by another person

sources.title: Toolkit: Community Plastic Clean-Up and Brand Audit
informs: protective gloves required
separate collection containers when possible
do not collect sharps; leave uncomfortable items and alert the group
adult supervision when children/youth participate

questions.text: Is this the litter concern you want help with?
In a sentence, what litter concern should we plan for?
Which city or neighborhood is this in?
How much time can you spend this week?
Will friends or an adult join you (not working alone if the site is near water or a road)?
Do you have sturdy work/gardening gloves and bags or buckets (or can you get them)?
Is the litter next to a river, canal, shore, or drain with water?
Do you see needles/syringes, other medical waste, oil drums, chemical containers, or strong chemical smells?
Does this action plan match what you see in your photo?

actions.title: Document litter hotspots (before photos + counts)
steps: In daylight, take clear before photos of each hotspot and note landmarks
If safe, count visible plastic items (bottles, bags, fragments) for a simple before metric
Do not touch unknown containers, oil drums, or anything that looks like medical waste

actions.title: Daylight buddy cleanup (ordinary litter only)
steps: Meet in daylight with at least one buddy; tell an adult where you are going
Wear closed-toe shoes and sturdy gloves; bring water and a basic first-aid kit if possible
Use gloves or tongs — never bare hands; keep hands away from face until gloves are off and hands washed
Collect only ordinary plastic and trash you can clearly identify
Use separate bags/buckets for recyclables vs residual waste when your area allows
Leave needles, syringes, medical waste, oil drums, and unknown chemicals in place — note the location and tell an adult or local authority
Take after photos and record bags collected / approximate item counts

actions.title: Safe drain-adjacent litter pickup (dry ground only)
steps: Stay on dry, stable ground — do not enter flowing water, culverts, or drainage outlets
With gloves, remove only loose ordinary litter around the grate that you can reach safely
Never put hands into drains, cavities, or deep openings
Skip the site if banks are steep/slippery, water is fast, or traffic is busy without an adult
Bag waste for proper disposal; note that clearing drainage litter helps keep plastic out of rivers

actions.title: Invite friends for a supervised practice cleanup
steps: Share the Iklim PAL invite card with 2–5 friends
Agree on daylight time, meeting point, who brings gloves/bags, and an adult contact
Brief everyone: gloves on, no bare hands, no medical/chemical waste, no entering water
Keep the message about community cleanup practice — not politics

stopConditions.userMessage: Stop DIY cleanup. Do not touch needles, syringes, medical waste, oil drums, or unknown chemical containers. Note the location and tell an adult or local authority so trained people can remove them safely.
Do not enter flood water, fast-flowing water, or unstable banks. Reschedule or ask adults/authorities for help.
Skip night or busy roadside cleanups without an adult and proper safety setup. Reschedule for daylight away from traffic risk.

Iklim PAL only covers safe youth plastic/river/drain litter actions in this pack. We could not match a pack-approved next step for your case. Do not invent DIY beyond this guide — ask an adult, teacher, or local authority for help, and stay away from hazards.

escalationDefaults.message: This needs an adult or local authority — not a youth DIY cleanup. Keep yourself and friends away from the hazard.
